newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures slide in line with dollar.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures slide in line with dollar.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium slid across the board in quiet trade on Monday as the dollar's fall against the yen triggered stop-loss selling, traders said.
"The strong yen led to stop-loss selling. But we've started to see bargain-hunters," a trader at a major trade house said adding that market sentiment was not bad.
In late Tokyo, the dollar was trading above 112 yen, compared with above 114 yen in the morning, hit by Japan's rising trade surplus and concerns about Asian currencies.
Benchmark June aluminium shed 1.9 yen to end at 186.9 yen, while April lost 0.8 yen to stand at 188.6.
Other contracts fell between 0.2 and 2.1 yen. Estimated volume was 1,366 lots.
In London on Friday, three-month aluminium finished up $1.50 at $1,607 in a generally sluggish market. The U.S. market was closed for Independence Day holiday.
